scope: Inspection of the linked trusted synchronous C callback controls and their production ownership gate. This is neither execution evidence nor a native validator.

tool.isolation: Already present image; pull disabled; network none; all container capabilities dropped; no new privileges; kernel directory mounted read-only.
tool.selection: Six complete numeric symbol ranges, including the cbpf_consume LL/SC continuation; linked-symbols.json records only the relevant function and data identities.

source_binding: The repository source, staged build source and prepared kernel source have identical SHA-256 values. Linked vmlinux and reviewed disassembly are bound separately above.

evidence: cbpf_dispatch_callbacks is at 0xffff800080e4aae0. ADRP/ADD at 0xffff800080e4aaf0 and 0xffff800080e4aaf4 resolve 0xffff800080e4ab78, the linked cbpf_ownership_callback.
The target is stored at 0xffff800080e4aafc, reloaded at 0xffff800080e4ab08 and 0xffff800080e4ab40, and invoked by BLR x8 at 0xffff800080e4ab14 and 0xffff800080e4ab4c.
findings.interpretation: The compiler specialized the known target identity but retained real indirect calls through the volatile slot.

findings.property: Full-capability transport across callback entry, logging and gate calls
evidence: 0xffff800080e4abe8 loads c2 from the selected context alias; 0xffff800080e4abec loads canonical c0; 0xffff800080e4abf8 compares exact capabilities; 0xffff800080e4ac1c checks the alias tag.
0xffff800080e4ac24 stores c2 to the capability stack slot before _printk at 0xffff800080e4ac44.

0xffff800080e4ac64 reloads c0 for operation 2 at 0xffff800080e4ac70; 0xffff800080e4ac84 reloads c0 for operation 3 at 0xffff800080e4ac90. Both BL targets resolve to cbpf_gate_impl at 0xffff80008003e260.
findings.interpretation: Each callback rereads the context capability. A full capability, rather than only its address, survives logging and the optional read before release.

evidence: cbpf_callback_check uses state at SP+0x60 and context at SP+0x30. Existing active state and nonbaseline refs are rejected at 0xffff800080e4a7ec and 0xffff800080e4a800.

0xffff800080e4a818 publishes the state through the per-CPU cbpf_active identity 0xffff800080eef830, before acquisition at 0xffff800080e4a848. 0xffff800080e4a84c stores returned c0 in a context alias slot.
0xffff800080e4a870 passes SP+0x30 to the dispatcher call at 0xffff800080e4a878. The dispatcher retains the same context in x20 and passes it again at 0xffff800080e4ab44.
0xffff800080e4abb4 reads the same per-CPU active invocation on callback entry; no callback arena allocation, reset or reacquisition occurs.

findings.property: Failure stops callback dispatch and protected continuation
evidence: 0xffff800080e4ab20 branches to the dispatcher epilogue on first false return. Completion increments at 0xffff800080e4ab28 through 0xffff800080e4ab38 follow success only.
0xffff800080e4ab54 branches back on later success only; false falls through to return. A failing second release therefore cannot dispatch the planned third callback.
0xffff800080e4ac78 branches to false return after a failed read, skipping release. The release return reflects state.failed at 0xffff800080e4ac94 through 0xffff800080e4ac9c.
Identity failure calls cbpf_fail at 0xffff800080e4acac, then returns false. cbpf_fail sets state.failed at 0xffff80008003e5d8 and performs only telemetry afterward.
findings.interpretation: Trusted result observation and cleanup remain reachable after failure; no additional callback or modeled protected operation does.

findings.property: Production membership and liveness checks precede the effect
evidence: cbpf_gate_impl loads cbpf_active at 0xffff80008003e298 and rejects missing, unentered or failed state at 0xffff80008003e2b4 through 0xffff80008003e2c4.
The canonical-view loop loads c2 at 0xffff80008003e31c and uses CHKEQ at 0xffff80008003e320. A missing member rejects through 0xffff80008003e488.
The matched private object is loaded at 0xffff80008003e3bc, its tag checked at 0xffff80008003e3c0 and an untagged object rejected at 0xffff80008003e3c4.
Only after those checks does operation 2 execute LDURSW through c0 at 0xffff80008003e3ec or operation 3 call the linked cbpf_consume at 0xffff80008003e414.
cbpf_consume clears the private object tag at 0xffff80008003e7c4 and stores the cleared capability at 0xffff80008003e7c8.

The later provider refcount address is cbpf_object+4, 0xffff800080f27e0c. The LSE decrement is LDADDL at 0xffff80008003e83c; the linked default branch selects the LL/SC sequence with LDXR at 0xffff80008003e8fc and STLXR at 0xffff80008003e904.
Both decrement sequences occur after the private invalidation store. No rejection path reaches either decrement.
findings.interpretation: This confirms sequential ordering in the linked implementation, not a concurrency or arbitrary reentrancy theorem.

evidence: Still-tagged cells alone reach trusted cleanup at 0xffff800080e4a94c.

Full-capability zero stores at 0xffff800080e4a9b4 through 0xffff800080e4a9c8 clear cell objects, canonical views and context aliases. The active invocation is cleared at 0xffff800080e4a9e0 before local_bh_enable at 0xffff800080e4a9fc.
findings.interpretation: This covers the named state slots, not erasure of all historical stack bytes.

limitations: No guest, payload or BPF program was executed for this review. Runtime observations must be cited from the separate trusted callback witness receipt.
The callback and dispatcher are trusted synchronous C code with bounded indices and no escaped handles. They are not protected BPF callback support or a general callback framework.

The trusted callback witness admits the first valid release and blocks subsequent use of that acquisition. It does not reproduce the original CVE-2022-50650 callback-frame policy, which forbids the initial caller-owned release.
The broader DDC, gateway and admission mediation premise remains trusted and is not discharged by this linked inspection.
